name: fill a grid with digits the sums leave no choice about
one_line: A crossword grid whose cells hold digits, so the crossings are settled by addition and nothing on the page has to be a word.
how: Print a two-by-two block of white cells with a sum written before each row and each column, the rule that every white cell holds a digit from 1 to 9, and the rule that no digit repeats inside a row or a column. Three and four across, four and three down, leave one filling out of the 6 561 possible. Then print the table that makes larger ones playable: the sums that can be written with only one set of digits, all thirty-four of them, from 3, 4, 16 and 17 on a row of two up to 45 on a row of nine. It is not a selection of the useful ones; it is every one there is, worked out from the subsets of 1 to 9.

knobs.knob: whether digits may repeat in a line
knobs.effect: Forbidden, a sum often fixes which digits are in a line and the grid can be built with one answer. Allowed, most sums admit several sets and no amount of crossing closes the grid.

knobs.knob: digits or letters in the cells
knobs.effect: Digits, and every step can be built, set and checked by machine, because nothing on the page is a word. Letters, and the same grid needs a word list to build and a dictionary to mark.

knobs.knob: whether the table of single-set sums is printed
knobs.effect: Printed, thirty-four entries in eight lines cover everything that trick can ever give, and a line carrying one of those sums is half done. Withheld, the same reasoning is redone on every line.

Sums written before each line keep the grid self-contained. Clues like «the seventh prime» or «27 times 79» make it a crossword whose answers are numbers, and then something outside the sheet has to be known.

where_the_work_is: In the sums, which have to leave one filling. On a small grid every filling can be counted, and counting them is the only thing that says whether the answer is one or several.
breaks: The half cells carrying the sums need a diagonal rule through them, and a hand-drawn diagonal scans badly, so print the rules. On 800x480 a two-by-two block fits in four rows of nineteen characters and one line of the table fits whole. Nothing here touches a letter inside a word, so this is the one form of its chapter that can be built, set and checked with no person anywhere in the loop.
